dedupe_keys.name: data on predictive resilience of interdependent water and transportation infrastructures a sociotechnical approach

description: The George Mason University authors publish processed data for assessing failures across connected water and transport networks in Tampa, Florida. The deposit covers random component failures and flooding associated with Hurricane Irma in 2017. It combines network resilience results with land-use and social-vulnerability information, and classifies geographical polygons using estimated flood-water levels. These data support comparisons of resilience prediction methods and coupled infrastructure failure simulations. Zenodo preserves version V.1.0 as one ZIP archive and provides a public download route. The repository assigns its Other (Open) licence category, so access is free, but the specific reuse conditions require checking before redistribution. The landing metadata do not specify numerical spatial resolution, internal file formats or a complete observation interval. No archive was downloaded. As a reviewer-assessed use, the dataset complements model-wntr with a water–transport resilience case; a working import into that model has not been demonstrated.
